meta.what: No-war price path per fuel (expected before the invasion), actual and no-war contract prices of the main buyers of Russian fuel, a corrected oil discount, and the formula that splits payments into a volume part at no-war prices and a war-time price windfall.
meta.bands: low / central / high = range of the pre-war forecasts (low = lowest forecast, high = mid-February 2022 futures with war-risk premium). 'actual' = the index the map uses now (energy2.json) or the same benchmark computed on the same base.

brent.what: Brent crude, EUR-based (USD path at actual ECB USD/EUR), base = 2019-2021 Brent in EUR

urals.what: Urals (Russian MinFin average, same base as energy2 price_index.urals): no-war Brent x pre-war Urals/Brent ratio 0.95 / 0.98 / 0.99

espo.what: ESPO Blend (China): pre-war ESPO traded at Dubai + 2-6 USD, about Brent; no-war = Brent x 0.97 / 1.00 / 1.04, base = Brent

diesel_gasoil_products.what: Russian oil-product basket incl. diesel/gasoil (same base as energy2 price_index.products): no-war Brent x pre-war products/Brent ratio x crack factor (2022 0.97/1.02/1.12, later 0.97/1.00/1.05)

lpg.what: LPG (propane/butane), priced off crude: no-war Brent x 0.90 / 1.00 / 1.10, base = Brent. Small: inside products/other_fossil on the map

ttf.what: European gas hub TTF (EUR/MWh), base 23.13 EUR/MWh (2019-2021)

jkm.what: Asian spot LNG (JKM; FRED PNGASJPUSDM used as the actual series): no-war = no-war TTF in USD + 0.5 USD/MMBtu

api2.what: API2 (ARA) coal: derived from Newcastle with the pre-war API2/Newcastle ratio (0.81), so its index equals Newcastle's; no free API2 futures archive found

russian_coal.what: Russian coal export price (same base as energy2 price_index.coal): moves with no-war Newcastle/API2

oil_formula_9m.what: An oil-indexed gas contract with a 9-month average lagged one month (annual value = half last year's, half this year's Brent), EUR-based

russian_pipeline_gas_europe.what: Russian pipeline gas in Europe, benchmark mix (same base as energy2 price_index.pipeline_gas): 0.75 TTF + 0.25 oil formula

russian_lng_europe.what: Russian LNG landed in Europe (same base as energy2 price_index.lng): moves with no-war TTF

HUN.contract_note: MVM-Gazprom 15-year contract signed Sep 2021 (4.5 bcm/yr, from Oct 2021). Formula not disclosed; customs unit values track TTF with a short lag (2022: 128 EUR/MWh vs TTF 122), so in practice hub-indexed rather than oil-capped. Deferred-payment arrangement for winter 2022/23 changes timing, not price.

SRB.contract_note: Srbijagas-Gazprom: 100% oil-indexed formula (2.2 bcm/yr contract signed May 2022, extended in 2025 at ~EUR 290/1000 m3 "under the same formula"); Serbia rejected a 30% oil / 70% hub mix. Supply via TurkStream-Bulgaria since Jan 2021 (Hungary route before).

SVK.contract_note: SPP-Gazprom long-term contract (to 2034), largely hub-indexed since the 2010s; after Ukraine transit ended (Jan 2025) gas arrives via TurkStream/Hungary.

AUT.contract_note: OMV-Gazprom Export contract (to 2040), hub-indexed; OMV terminated the contract in Dec 2024 after an arbitration award, so Austrian imports from Russia ended with Ukraine transit on 1 Jan 2025.

TUR.contract_note: BOTAS-Gazprom (Blue Stream 16 bcm/yr and TurkStream-1 contracts, ~22 bcm/yr, extended year by year since 2025) plus private importers (Western line, ~5.75 bcm). Oil-indexed with negotiated discounts (10.25% in 2015-16, renewed demands 2021-2023) and a deferred-payment arrangement in 2022-2024 that shifts cash timing but not the contract price. Small Russian LNG cargoes 2022-2024.
TUR.urals_note: Turkey's crude price is MinFin Urals plus Black Sea freight (turkey_prices.json), so its discount to Brent is the full Urals discount; Turkish pipeline gas uses turkey_prices.json (70% hub / 30% oil since the 2021 renegotiation, pre-war, so the no-war contract keeps that mix).

CHN.contract_note: CNPC-Gazprom Power of Siberia 30-year contract (38 bcm/yr plateau reached Dec 2024), oil-product-linked with a ~9-month lag, base price undisclosed; Russian LNG (Yamal, Sakhalin, Arctic LNG 2 from 2024) bought on term and spot.
CHN.espo_note: No buyer-level ESPO price series was found free of charge. Platts: ESPO Blend traded at +4.5 to +6 USD/bbl over Dubai in Sep-Oct 2021 and premiums 'beat estimates' in Jan 2022; at a discount to Brent in Jun-Jul 2024; at -9 USD/bbl to Dubai after the Jan 2025 US sanctions. China's customs unit value (crude_cif_usd_bbl, includes pipeline ESPO and seaborne Urals) shows only a small discount to Brent (-0.7 to +8.6 USD/bbl), so the map's own Chinese crude index (prices.json) is better than any benchmark; no-war ESPO = Brent x 0.97/1.00/1.04 (nowar_index.espo).

BLR.contract_note: Gazprom-Beltransgaz (Gazprom Transgaz Belarus) price set by intergovernmental protocol: $127 (2019-2020), $128.5 (2021), frozen at $128.52 for 2022 and, per Russian Economy Minister Reshetnikov, fixed at $128.5 for 2024-2025; settled in roubles since 2023. 2026: no published change, assumed unchanged.

ARM.contract_note: Gazprom Armenia (100% Gazprom) buys at a political border price of $165/1000 m3 (since Jan 2019), unchanged through 2026.

KAZ.contract_note: QazaqGaz-Gazprom swap and processing arrangements (Karachaganak gas sent to Orenburg and Russian gas returned to southern Kazakhstan), plus since 2023 transit-linked purchases; prices are swap settlement values, not commercial prices.

UZB.contract_note: Uzbekneftegaz-Gazprom deal (Oct 2023, via Kazakhstan, ~$160/1000 m3), volumes rising to ~5.5 bcm in 2024.

MDA.contract_note: Moldovagaz-Gazprom: until Oct 2021 a "European formula" (Gazprom far-abroad price over the previous 9 months), from Nov 2021 a 5-year contract linked to TTF and oil, with prices set monthly (record $1,195 in Apr 2022). Right-bank Moldova stopped buying Gazprom gas in Dec 2022/early 2023; Transnistria's gas was unpaid and ended 1 Jan 2025.

BGR.contract_note: Bulgargaz-Gazprom Export contract (2013-2022), oil-indexed with partial hub indexation after the 2019-2020 EC commitments; Gazprom cut supply on 27 Apr 2022. From 2023 only small volumes recorded as Russian origin (TurkStream gas bought by traders).

GRC.contract_note: DEPA-Gazprom contract to 2026, oil-indexed with growing hub component after the 2020 arbitration (DEPA won a retroactive price revision). Russian pipeline gas via TurkStream/Bulgaria.

BIH.contract_note: Energoinvest (Federation) and Gas-Res (Republika Srpska) contracts with Gazprom, priced quarterly on the 9-month change in oil-product prices, paid in EUR.

MKD.contract_note: North Macedonia: GA-MA/ESM purchases of Russian gas (via Bulgaria) with partial hub linkage; volumes falling as Greek/Bulgarian LNG-based supply grows.

DEU.contract_note: Uniper, RWE, Wingas/SEFE, EnBW/VNG: Gazprom Export contracts largely hub-indexed (NCG/Gaspool/TTF) after the 2010-2016 renegotiations; Nord Stream deliveries stopped 31 Aug 2022.

ITA.contract_note: Eni and other Italian buyers: hub-indexed Gazprom contracts (renegotiated 2013-2016 to TTF/PSV); supply fell sharply after 2022 and ended with Ukraine transit in Jan 2025 except small traces.

CZE.contract_note: Hub-indexed supply via Germany and Slovakia (RWE/innogy, Vemex). Ukraine-route transit ended 1 Jan 2025.

POL.contract_note: PGNiG-Gazprom Yamal contract (to end-2022, ~10 bcm/yr). The Stockholm tribunal (Mar 2020) replaced the oil-linked price formula with one tied to Western European market prices, retroactive from Nov 2014; Gazprom stopped deliveries on 27 Apr 2022.

FIN.contract_note: LNG: small-scale cargoes (Pori/Tornio). Pipeline: Gasum-Gazprom contract, hub-related after Gasum's 2020 arbitration win; supply cut 21 May 2022.

KGZ.contract_note: Gazprom Kyrgyzstan (100% Gazprom) imports at a political price (~$150-180/1000 m3).

JPN.contract_note: Sakhalin-2 long-term LNG contracts (JERA, Tokyo Gas, Kyushu, Hiroshima Gas, Tohoku), oil-indexed (JCC slope ~14-15%), plus some Yamal spot; continued after 2022 under Japanese exemptions.

KOR.contract_note: KOGAS Sakhalin-2 term contract (1.5 Mt/yr, oil-indexed, to 2028) plus spot Yamal/Sakhalin cargoes.

IND.urals_note: Customs CIF (Comtrade/DGCI&S via prices.json) includes freight, which rose sharply in 2022-2023, so the CIF discount to Brent (6.8 USD in 2022, 7.9 in 2023, 2.3 in 2024) is smaller than the FOB discount (energy.json: Brent minus CREA realised 19.5 / 17.2 / 12.3 USD). India's CIF price above Brent in 2025-2026 should be checked in prices.json (2026 = Jan-Aug, Hormuz spike months weigh heavily).

switching_cost_r7.status: switching premium unchanged (already measured against the same year's Russian realised price, not 2019-2021); only oil_discount_gain is corrected to the no-war discount

windfall_impact.note: central p (actual) with low/central/high no-war n; builder ranges will be wider once p bands are combined. EUR bn, 2022-2026 (2026 = Jan-Aug). Ranked by fuel paid to Russia 2022-2026.

formula.identity: actual payment - expected payment = (actual volume - expected volume) x no-war price + actual volume x (actual price - no-war price)

symbols.A_i: to_rus.years[i] x fsy_i: fuel paid in year i (fsy_i from fuel_share_year(), else the pre-war share moved to the year's prices, as now)
symbols.n_i: no-war fuel price level, 2019-2021 = 1 (new: nowar_fuel_index(iso3), below)
symbols.V_i: A_i / p_i: actual fuel volume at 2019-2021 prices
symbols.E_i: base x FRAC_i x bmul_i x fs: expected fuel volume at 2019-2021 prices (fs = fossil_share(iso3))

parts.volume_part_fuel: (E_i - V_i) x n_i  -> 'less (or more) paid to Russia', fuel volumes now valued at no-war prices
parts.windfall_new: A_i x (1 - n_i / p_i) = V_i x (p_i - n_i)  -> 'extra paid because of war-time prices'; replaces A_i x (1 - 1/p_i)
parts.check: E_i x n_i - A_i = (E_i - V_i) x n_i - V_i x (p_i - n_i): exact, no residual
parts.non_fuel: unchanged: non-fuel volumes keep 2019-2021 prices and no windfall (their price rise is general inflation)

nowar_fuel_index: where prices.json windfall_parts has fuel payments for the year: n_i / p_i = sum over fuels f of s_f x (N_f / p_f), with s_f the fuel's share of that year's fuel payments; p_f = own customs index (own_index, crude/products/coal) or the benchmark idx(); N_f = nowar_index (crude -> urals, products and other_fossil -> diesel_gasoil_products, coal -> russian_coal)

pipeline gas and LNG use the ratio method: N_gas / p_gas = F(no-war inputs) / F(actual inputs) for the country's contract formula (contract_prices.*.formula_weights: hub = TTF, oil9 = 9-month oil formula, oil3 = 3-month oil formula for Asian LNG, jkm = spot; fixed-price buyers BLR, ARM, KGZ, UZB, KAZ, AZE, GEO get 1, i.e. no windfall)
otherwise the pre-war mix: n_i = sum m_f N_f / sum m_f with the same weights as fuel_index(); gas N = gas_index(iso3) x F0/F
n_i = p_i x (n_i / p_i); 2019-2021 keep n = 1 (no windfall before the war, as now)
builder_steps: add NOWAR = load(GAPS / 'energy_nowar.json') and nowar_fuel_index(iso3, band) as above

war_windfall(): vals.append(tr['years'][i] x fsy x (1 - n[i] / fuel[i])) instead of (1 - 1 / fuel[i]); low = low p with high n, high = high p with low n; keep the re-sorting; ALLOW NEGATIVE values (years where Russia sold below the no-war price, e.g. China 2025) or floor at 0 - owner decision
price_indices(): to_rus keeps its pidx for actual values but the fuel part must be valued at n: pidx_r7 = 1 / (fsy x n / fuel + (1 - fsy) / nonfuel), so value / pidx_r7 = V_fuel x n + V_nonfuel

expected side: add a per-series multiplier nmul_i = fs x n_i + (1 - fs) (1 in 2021) and either (a) write bmul x nmul into bmul/bmul_lo/bmul_hi (no site change), or (b) keep nmul as its own field and multiply it in exV() in calc() (one line in site/index.html, clearer); (b) is recommended
check_data.py check 12 still holds (2019-2021 unchanged); add a check that windfall + fuel volume part = E x n - A for every country-year
formula.fuel_share_note: fsy is the share of the year's payments that was fuel at actual prices; fs (pre-war) weights the expected side. Using fsy for the actual side and fs for the expected side keeps the identity exact for the fuel part, because only V (from A and p) and E (from base and bmul) enter it.
formula.currency: All indices EUR-based at actual ECB USD/EUR, like energy2.json, so the windfall measures commodity prices, not the euro's fall in 2022. Converting the no-war USD paths at the pre-war expected rate (1.13 in ECB Dec 2021 and EC Winter 2022 assumptions) would lower n by 7% in 2022 and 4% in 2023-2024 and raise the windfall correspondingly.

This repository: energy2.json price_index and levels, gas_prices.json, prices.json, turkey_prices.json, energy.json, site/data.json (to_rus, windfall), pipeline/build_data.py functions

notes: Generated 2026-10-18 (round 7, energy_nowar). Produced by the project's research step and kept as a data input; the research scripts are not in the repository, and the sources are listed in the notes.

Choice: central = the median of the institutional forecasts and futures dated October 2021 to January 2022 (oil), or the mean of the institutional forecasts and the early/mid-January 2022 futures (gas, coal); low = the lowest pre-war source (mostly October 2021 forecasts, before the Q4-2021 gas squeeze); high = the mid-February 2022 futures, which already held a war-risk premium (TTF Cal-23 rose from ~43 in mid-January to ~52-56 in mid-February and 57-63 on 22-23 February; Brent rose ~10 USD).

2025-2026 lie beyond most pre-war horizons: oil from the World Bank October 2021 path and the Nov 2021 / Jan 2022 futures curves extended at their slope; gas from World Bank and curve extrapolation; certainty D.
Coal futures (Newcastle, API2) for early 2022 are approximate (no free archive found); certainty D. API2 is derived from Newcastle with the pre-war ratio.

2026 actual prices include the Hormuz-crisis spike (Brent > 100 USD in Mar-May 2026), which is not caused by Russia's war but counts as windfall against an ex-ante no-war path; see the owner decisions in the notes file.

Gas contract no-war prices use the ratio method: the country's actual price x (formula at no-war inputs / formula at actual inputs), so contract levels, premiums and discounts that are not war-related are kept.

energy.json's low gas switching premium uses FRED PNGASJPUSDM as 'Japan LNG (oil-indexed long-term contracts)', but that series averages 33.3 USD/MMBtu in 2022 (TTF 37.5), i.e. it behaves like spot JKM, not an oil-indexed contract price (World Bank Japan LNG was about half that). Worth checking separately.
